content.text:
All 48 tests pass, 3 remain as `it.todo`.

🟢 Green Phase Complete:

**Implementation**: Added a `rejectOverclaimedTypes` guard in `entitledPayoutOf`, running before the sum. It counts damage entries per `itemType` and compares against the count of insured items of that type, throwing `More <type> damages claimed than the policy insures` when the claim exceeds coverage.

**Result**: All tests now pass (48 passing, 3 todo)

**Approach**: Why this is minimal:
- The check lives at the seam named in the brief (`entitledPayoutOf`), before summing, so nothing about `damagePayoutOf` or the payout arithmetic changed.
- `countOfType` is a plain `filter().length` — no map/grouping structure was introduced, since the test only needs a per-type comparison of two small lists.
- The `countOfType(insuredTypes, type) > 0` clause was added only because a test forced it. My first version fired for uninsured types too, which broke the existing "Item not covered by the policy: amulet" test — an uninsured type has 0 insured items, so every claim on it trivially "overclaims". The guard restricts the new rule to types the policy actually insures and leaves the coverage check to `insuredItemOfType`, as it did before.
- The existing two-swords/two-entries case stays green without special handling: 2 entries against 2 insured swords is not greater, so the guard is silent.

Files:
- `/home/experimenter/experiments/runs/2026-07-26_11-43-59_claim-office-example-mapping_v4-exact-subagents_opus-5-no-thinking/src/claim-office.ts`
- `/home/experimenter/experiments/runs/2026-07-26_11-43-59_claim-office-example-mapping_v4-exact-subagents_opus-5-no-thinking/src/claim-office.spec.ts`

One note for the Refactor phase: the two error checks are now ordered by an implicit dependency — `rejectOverclaimedTypes` must skip uninsured types because `insuredItemOfType` owns that error. That coupling is currently expressed only by the `> 0` clause and a comment; it may be worth making explicit.

Proceeding to Refactor phase.
